name: PixelCard-TS-TW

frames.best_why: The Default card is fully covered by the dense pale pixel grid, the clearest view of the effect at full bloom.

tagline: Tiny pixels bloom across a card when the pointer enters.
summary: Three dark rounded cards sit side by side, each with a title and a hint to hover. On hover a field of small squares swells across the card and shimmers until the pointer leaves.
appearance: Three near-black rounded cards in a row, each centred with a small title, a muted subtitle and a pill reading 'Hover me'. A hovered card fills with a dense grid of tiny pale squares.
behaviour: Hovering a card sprouts a field of small pixels from the centre outward, which keep pulsing in size while the pointer stays. Leaving makes them shrink away and leaves the plain card.
demo_content: Three cards titled Default, Blue and Pink with subtitles 'Neutral pixels', 'Cool tones' and 'Warm glow'.
search_phrases: card that fills with tiny squares on hover
canvas particle card for a feature
dots that shimmer over a panel
retro pixel animation on a card
use_when: A feature or teaser card should reward hover with a tactile pixel flourish.
avoid_when: The pixels are decorative only, and the whole effect needs a pointer or keyboard focus to appear.
customise: Variant (default, blue, yellow, pink), pixel gap, speed, colour list and whether the card is focusable are props; size and border come from classes.
weight_why: Thousands of tiny canvas squares are redrawn every frame while a card is hovered.

a11y.note: It honours reduced-motion, but the card has no role or instructions, so the focus-triggered animation is unexplained.

issues: At full bloom the pixel field crowds the card's title and subtitle, making them harder to read.
polish_why: A neat pixel bloom with three colour variants; the dot field crowds the text at full coverage.
